**ID:** Snp 5.9 (PTS Snp 209)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Hemakamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Hemaka") constitutes the ninth discourse of the *Pārāyanavagga*, the fifth chapter of the *Suttanipāta* (Snp 5.9, PTS Snp 209) [Anderson & Smith 1913]. In the collection's sequential numbering, its verses begin at verse 1084, framing a dialogue in verse between the Buddha and the student Hemaka (*icc-āyasmā Hemako*) [Norman 1997–2001; Anderson & Smith 1913]. The text centers on the inquiry of how one crosses over entanglements and desire in the world.
